text: Counts on and back in steps of ones, tens and hundreds from any number up to 1000, and extends a number sequence, saying its rule, such as 'add 3 each time'.
Reads and writes numbers below zero, such as −5 °C, places them on a number line, and compares and orders positive and negative numbers using =, > and <.
Reads and writes numbers to 1000 in figures and words, says what each digit is worth, and partitions a 3-digit number into hundreds, tens and ones in more than one way.
Finds the missing number in an addition or subtraction with numbers to 1000, such as 245 + □ = 400, using the inverse operation, and checks that both sides of = are the same.

Adds and subtracts numbers to 1000 mentally, using complements and near-hundreds, and in columns, exchanging in any column including across zeros, choosing the quicker way and checking with an estimate.
Sorts numbers to 1000 into odd and even by their ones digit, and explains what happens when two odd, two even, or one odd and one even number are added or subtracted.
Says and uses the times tables to 10 × 10 (Pahade), finds multiples of 2, 5 and 10 up to 1000, and finds the factor pairs of a number using the tables.
Multiplies mentally by 10 using place value, and by 2, 3, 4 and 5 by doubling or by splitting a number into tens and ones, such as 4 × 23 = 80 + 12.
Multiplies a 2- or 3-digit number by a 1-digit number in columns, carrying when a column's product is ten or more, after estimating the answer.
Shows and names a fraction as equal parts of a shape or object that together make one whole, such as three-quarters, and explains why more parts make each part smaller.
Places halves, quarters, fifths and tenths on a number line from 0 to 1, and uses the line to compare and order fractions with the same denominator.
Finds a half, quarter, three-quarters, third or tenth of a quantity or set of objects, such as ¾ of 12 sweets, by sharing into equal groups or dividing.
Reads, writes and partitions numbers to 10 000 in figures and words, and says what each digit is worth.
Reads and writes numbers in Roman numerals, such as XIV, and compares them with the Indian place value system, which has a zero and needs no new symbols.
Rounds a 3-digit number to the nearest 10 or 100, and a 4-digit number to the nearest 1000, and uses rounding to estimate an answer before calculating.
Finds the rule of a linear sequence, such as 7, 11, 15, …, uses it to find the next and missing terms, and makes up a sequence from a given rule.
Recalls every multiplication fact to 10 × 10 (Pahade) quickly, and uses a known fact to find a related one, such as 7 × 8 from 7 × 4.
Multiplies a 2-digit number by a 1-digit number by partitioning it into tens and ones, with a grid or area model and in an expanded layout, and explains why each way gives the same answer.
Divides a number up to 100 by a 1-digit number by grouping, by jumping back on a number line and by short division, and checks the answer by multiplying.
Solves word problems of two or more steps with numbers to 1000 by drawing a bar model of the story, choosing each operation from what happens in it, and checking the answer makes sense.
Reads and writes amounts in rupees and paise, such as ₹45.50, makes an amount from notes and coins in more than one way, and reads prices in another currency that uses a decimal point.
Adds and subtracts amounts of money in rupees and paise, with and without exchanging, and finds the change from a note.
Solves one- and two-step problems about buying and selling in rupees, such as the total of a simple bill or the change from ₹500, choosing the operation from the story.
Finds the change from a payment, and plans how to spend a fixed amount on a few items, saying how much is left after each one.
Identifies whether a number pattern grows, such as 3, 6, 9, 12, or repeats, such as 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, and extends it.
Says the rule of a sequence in words, such as 'add 3 each time', and uses a given rule to write the next terms from any starting number.
Finds the missing inputs and outputs in a table for a one-step rule, such as 'multiply by 2', and says the rule from a completed table.
Finds missing numbers in a linear sequence or a rule table by working out the rule, and checks the answer against the numbers either side.
Recalls addition facts to 20 and multiplication facts to 10 × 10 quickly and accurately, and improves on their own earlier time.
Chooses a mental strategy for a calculation, such as bridging through 100, adjusting a near-hundred or doubling, uses it, and explains why it was quicker than columns.
